messages:
jules: Heads-up — design ask: can we show a mini cost-forecast hovercard on the SKU hover in the Console? idea is to preview per-model marginal cost + estimated cache savings if you change routing policy or enable sticky routing. quick mock attached (not in thread).

sam: +1 for previewing econ impact before people flip routing. saves tickets. :thumbsup:

katie: curious — do we mean an instantaneous delta (current day) or a forecast window (7d/30d)? needs to match billing windows.

jules: 7d by default with a small confidence band. UX should call it a "preview" and not promise billing. also show which tokens are modeled (gen vs emb).

pranav: important note: cache savings depend heavily on sequence shapes. we can approximate with current traffic histograms but we need to show sample-rate and variance. otherwise ops will complain.

maria: If we add this, product wants a quick API endpoint so other tools (support, SRE runbooks) can fetch the same preview. internal only.

sam: sketch for API: GET /internal/console/cost_preview?route_id=R123&policy=sticky&window=7d
suggested response: 200 {
  "model_summaries": [...],
  "total_delta_tokens": "-12.3k",
  "estimated_cost_delta_cents": "-24.5"
}

pranav: pls avoid exposing raw cent numbers for multi-tenant queries. we should return per-tenant-unit metrics and use a transformer to render currency in UI. also include metadata: sample_rate, sequence_shape_bucket.

katie: from UX side, we need two things on hover: short headline (e.g., "~$0.25/day saved"), and an expandable microbreakdown (per-model, cache vs model-run). headline must round and include confidence.

jules: agreement — also add a tiny link to "view assumptions" that opens a modal with the exact sampling windows and hedging rules.

maria: ops-bot FYI: will this increase telemetry volume? we might generate a lot of preview calls during rollouts. ops-bot, can we throttle by user and cache previews for 1m?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: throttling recommended. we have a 1m LRU cache available at /internal/cache-preview with 64k entries. requests must send X-Internal-Key header. :robot_face:

pranav: pro tip: cache keys should include route_id, policy, sample_rate, and client_timezone. otherwise preview differences look confusing.

sam: one more API detail — include a decision path ID for routing policy so we can tie preview to telemetry later (for A/B comparison). call it decision_id.

katie: UX question: should previews show amortized GPU time vs per-token cost? product prefers both, but maybe hide GPU time under advanced view.

jules: hide GPU time behind 'show advanced metrics'. headline stays simple.

maria: engineering ask: what's the acceptable staleness for the preview? 10s? 1m? that affects cache TTL choices.

pranav: 30s should be fine for most routes. heavy routes can be sampled less frequently. include a cache-hit indicator in the hovercard (fresh/stale).

sam: small implementation note: reuse the existing econ microservice that already computes per-invocation token attribution. add a lightweight aggregation endpoint that approximates 7d deltas rather than running full rollups.

maria: rollouts team: when we enable the hovercard, ops wants a toggle to opt-out per-org (privacy/regulatory). add feature flagging.

jules: noted. final UX ask: when the user modifies policy in the same modal, have the hovercard update in-place and show a tiny 'apply' button that snapshots the preview to the rollout flow.

pranav: technical caveat — applying sticky routing can change cache locality dramatically. the preview needs a 'potential warmup' line showing expected short-term negative delta until caches warm up.

katie: we'll design a small timeline sparkline for that warmup window (0-24h).

sam: ok action items: 1) prana/eng: prototype API and cache; 2) sam/frontend: hovercard mock + interactions; 3) product: finalize copy; 4) ops: quota/throttle rules.

maria: i'll open a GH issue with acceptance criteria and link the mock.

jules: thanks — ping me when GH issue is up. this should reduce surprise burn during routing experiments. :party_popper:
